jobs.title: Command Mission Operations Lead
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

America is under sustained cyber attack. Our adversaries infiltrate our networks, steal our IP, and degrade the digital infrastructure that modern life runs on. They’ve learned—correctly—that those attacks rarely produce consequences.

Twenty was founded to change that, by making our adversaries think twice before they attack us. Our vision is American and allied primacy in cyberspace—a future where they cannot contest us, deterrence is assured, and the free world remains secure.

Founded in 2024, Twenty Technologies (www.twenty.io http://www.twenty.io) industrializes offensive cyber operations for the U.S. and its allies. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Twenty has raised $168M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Caffeinated Capital, Friends & Family Capital, Point72 Ventures, General Catalyst, and In-Q-Tel.

 
 

Mission | On Site | Full Time | Active TS/SCI with Full Scope Polygraph

 
 


ROLE SUMMARY

Twenty builds AI-native software for offensive cyber teams operating in complex mission environments. We are looking for a Command Mission Operations Lead to own how Twenty’s capabilities and delivery team integrate with current state and future state cyber weapons systems to maximize cyber force generation. You are a cyber warfare professional whose judgement and reputation are widely respected in the community. You will be the trusted face of Twenty with mission and task force leadership who is able to provide both tactical and strategic advice on force and capability employment against persistent nation state cyber threats.

This is a mission adoption and operational leadership role, not a quota-based sales role.

This role is for someone who has directly commanded cyber operations or advised command or JFHQ-level senior leadership on force employment, and is credible with operators and analysts at the tactical level.

 

The people who do this well have usually been an O-5/O-6, a Warrant Officer, or a GS-14/15 inside a national cyber or intelligence organization — in command, operations, or senior advisory roles where they owned mission outcomes rather than briefed them. You know how targeting, authorities, tasking, and assessment actually work, because you have driven the machinery.

You will translate a defined company strategy into an executable plan for your accounts, and you will lead the people to execute it. Deployment Managers and Forward Deployed Analysts are assigned to your lines of effort — you decide how they are resourced, what they work on, and what good looks like, and you are accountable for the outcomes that team delivers.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Execution against account strategy

 - Translate company strategy into the deployment and operationalization plan for a portfolio of accounts within a command — approach, growth, training model, and staffing posture — built from scratch where none exists.

 - Direct a team of Deployment Managers and Forward Deployed Analysts assigned to your account: set their lines of effort, resource them to mission priority, hold the standard, and own what the team delivers.

 - Own the framing and positioning for renewal and growth conversations, using account-wide engagement metrics and competitive context to make the case.

Serve as a trusted advisor to senior leadership

 - Serve as Twenty's primary interface to task force and command leadership (O-5, O-6, GS-15): what the product is doing for the mission, where it goes next, and how it changes force employment.

 - Build and sustain a champion network across the account, from mission team and task force technical leads up to commanders and their senior civilians, and turn those relationships into deep cross-functional advocacy.

 - Brief senior leadership (SES, GOFO) on mission impact serving their priorities — operational outcomes, force generation, and resourcing.

Define successful force and capability employment across an organization

 - Shape the account's training strategy and the systems that scale it: standard curricula, train-the-trainer models, and institutional channels (J7 curriculum, JQR standards) that outlive any one engagement.

 - Translate mission requirements into product direction — own the engagement strategy for new capability from alpha through production release, and mentor your team on how to diagnose the true capability gaps and requirements that Twenty is postured to address.

 - Understand and orient your team and company leadership to what is true in the ambiguous field operating picture across the portfolio: users, stakeholders, workflows, blockers, adoption signals, risks, and value stories.

 - Mentor the Deployment and Forward Deployed Analyst team, and help set the talent bar as the team scales.
   
    


WHO YOU ARE

You came out of CYBERCOM, SOCOM, NSA, or CIA — most likely as an O-5/O-6, a Warrant Officer, or a GS-14/15. You held a command, a task force deputy or operations role, a technical directorate, or a senior advisory seat where the mission outcome was yours to answer for.

 - 12+ years in offensive cyber, cyber operations, or intelligence operations, including 5+ years in a leadership or senior advisory role at USCYBERCOM, NSA, or CIA.

 - Leader or technical director of a cyber mission element, task force, or operations directorate — CNMF, a JFHQ-C, a CMT/CST construct, an NSA operations or technical directorate, or a CIA or SOCOM equivalent.

 - Track record of advising a commander or senior executives on operational employment: what to task, what to accept, what to stop, and what the authorities allowed.

 - Owned targeting, mission planning, execution support, or assessment at a level where you shaped the campaign, not just the engagement.

 - Sat in requirements, capability development, or acquisition conversations and know how a capability actually reaches an operator — and where that path usually breaks.

 - Ability to learn complex software quickly and explain it credibly to operators, targeters, program staff, and flag-level leadership.

 - Strong written communication. You turn ambiguous field input into concise requirements, decision memos, and executive-ready summaries.

 - Prior experience in a commercial product, deployment, or capability-delivery role supporting national security customers is a plus, not a requirement.

You are technically credible without being the engineer in the room. Operators respect you because you have been one or led them; leadership listens to you because you tell them the uncomfortable part first. You are comfortable operating with wide latitude — you build the plan, then run it.


Occasional travel for customer engagements, training, and mission support is required.



Benefits 
What's on the table:

 - Health. Medical, dental, and vision plan options. Life / AD&D, disability coverage options.

 - Family. Paid parental leave for eligible full-time employees. 12 weeks for birthing parents, 4 for non-birthing parents, 6 weeks for adoptive, foster, or intended parents through surrogacy.

 - Vacation. Paid holidays and flexible PTO. Take what you need.

 - Retirement. 401(k) with pre-tax and Roth options. HSA/FSA options, dependent care FSA.

Benefits vary by location, role, and eligibility. Full plan details provided during the interview and offer process.





If this role sounds like you, apply and share with us your interest

Due to U.S. government contract and security requirements, this role is limited to U.S. citizens. Some positions may also require eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance. Any active clearance requirement will be listed in the role description.

Twenty is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, veteran status, disability, or any other protected status, consistent with applicable law.

If you need a reasonable accommodation during the hiring process, let us know and we will work with you.

jobs.title: Strategic Finance and Business Operations Associate
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

America is under sustained cyber attack. Our adversaries infiltrate our networks, steal our IP, and degrade the digital infrastructure that modern life runs on. They’ve learned—correctly—that those attacks rarely produce consequences.

Twenty was founded to change that, by making our adversaries think twice before they attack us. Our vision is American and allied primacy in cyberspace—a future where they cannot contest us, deterrence is assured, and the free world remains secure.

Founded in 2024, Twenty Technologies (www.twenty.io http://www.twenty.io) industrializes offensive cyber operations for the U.S. and its allies. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Twenty has raised $168M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Caffeinated Capital, Friends & Family Capital, Point72 Ventures, General Catalyst, and In-Q-Tel.

 
 

Mission | On Site | Full Time | U.S. Citizenship Required / No Active Clearance Required

 




ROLE SUMMARY

The Finance and Operations team focuses on some of Twenty’s most critical business problems with a high degree of visibility into the entire organization. The team is responsible for annual planning, resource allocation, performing financial analysis, and acting as a business partner with leaders across the company. This role requires someone who is highly analytical and strategic, a great communicator, a structured problem solver, and level-headed when faced with ambiguity.

This role is ideal for a former banker, investor, or startup finance operator who wants to skip business school and jump into a high-velocity generalist seat from the ground floor. You are eager to stop spreading comps and start building a company.

 


WHAT YOU'LL OWN (CORE RESPONSIBILITIES)

 - The Model. Build and own Twenty's financial model end-to-end. Drive annual planning, the headcount ledger, board reporting, and the analytical engine the company uses to make decisions. When investors ask questions in the next fundraise, your modeling work is what helps answer them.

 - FP&A & Reporting. Run semi-annual budgeting and ongoing headcount planning. Stand up the reporting infrastructure that gives every function visibility into how it's actually performing. Translate the financials into something team leaders can act on.

 - Fundraising & Investor Relations. Partner with the Founders and VP Finance on the next fundraise. Build the data room and own diligence. Between rounds, own monthly executive updates and quarterly board reporting.

 - The Operating Cadence. Run the systems that keep a company moving: compensation design, offer generation, performance structure, and spend policies.

 - Special Projects. Some examples are real estate, market research, vendor strategy, software procurement.

 


WHO YOU ARE

 - 1–5 years in investment banking, private equity, or strategic finance at a top-tier startup.

 - Mastery with Excel and Google Sheets. You can build a highly legible three-statement model, and you can layer in scenario modeling to answer urgent questions.

 - Detail-obsessed. You believe formatting is a tool for cross-functional communication, not a chore. You sweat the small stuff because small mistakes can compound.

 - High horsepower. You dive in head first, whether it’s a one-page memo for the CEO, a slide for the Board, or an offer package for a new hire.

 - Urgency. You don't wait for directions—you figure things out. You create your own urgency, whether it is because the status quo frustrates you or because you see the path to a better end state.

 - Generalist by instinct. You enjoy a wide problem space. You apply first principles across finance, hiring, contracts, and ops because the underlying skill is the same: think clearly, move fast, get to the answer.

 - In-person builder. You want to spend your career around kind and smart people—refining your craft while advancing a critical mission.

 


NICE TO HAVE

 - Industry Experience. Prior background or interest in software, AI, cyber, defense, or intelligence.

 - AI Pilled. Daily ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini user. Use Claude Code or Cowork, Rogo, Hebbia, or equivalent AI tools. You see agents as the way to automate routine tasks and as the future of work.

 - Sense of Humor. Nano Banana image generation ability.



Benefits 
What's on the table:

 - Health. Medical, dental, and vision plan options. Life / AD&D, disability coverage options.

 - Family. Paid parental leave for eligible full-time employees. 12 weeks for birthing parents, 4 for non-birthing parents, 6 weeks for adoptive, foster, or intended parents through surrogacy.

 - Vacation. Paid holidays and flexible PTO. Take what you need.

 - Retirement. 401(k) with pre-tax and Roth options. HSA/FSA options, dependent care FSA.

Benefits vary by location, role, and eligibility. Full plan details provided during the interview and offer process.

jobs.title: Senior Recruiter, GTM & Customer Success
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE COMPANY

America is under sustained cyber attack. Our adversaries infiltrate our networks, steal our IP, and degrade the digital infrastructure that modern life runs on. They’ve learned—correctly—that those attacks rarely produce consequences.

Twenty was founded to change that, by making our adversaries think twice before they attack us. Our vision is American and allied primacy in cyberspace—a future where they cannot contest us, deterrence is assured, and the free world remains secure.

Founded in 2024, Twenty Technologies (www.twenty.io http://www.twenty.io) industrializes offensive cyber operations for the U.S. and its allies. Headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, Twenty has raised $168M from Khosla Ventures, Accel, Caffeinated Capital, Friends & Family Capital, Point72 Ventures, General Catalyst, and In-Q-Tel.

 


ROLE SUMMARY

Twenty builds AI-native offensive cyber and mission software for the U.S. government and its allies. As Senior Recruiter, GTM & Customer Success, you’ll build the teams that bring those capabilities to customers and missions: the people who open new opportunities, build trusted partnerships, and turn customer needs into lasting mission impact.

You’ll own sourcing-heavy recruiting across Sales, Growth, business development, government relations, partnerships, and customer/mission-facing leadership. Working directly with business and mission leaders, you’ll help define what each hire needs to accomplish, shape candidate profiles and assessment plans, and advise on scope, level, and market realities. From the first outreach through the close, you’ll turn those priorities into exceptional hires.

This is a chance to shape both who joins Twenty and how we build relationships in the markets we serve. You’ll develop trusted networks across cyber, defense, national security, and cleared talent communities, where credibility, discretion, and sustained engagement matter. We’re looking for someone with recruiting experience in defense technology, cyber, or companies serving government and national security customers—someone who brings curiosity, sound judgment, and urgency, and can turn a specialized search into a clear plan, a strong pipeline, and a successful hire.




WHO YOU ARE

 - You have a sourcing-first mindset and turn cold outreach into real pipelines and hires.

 - You bring strong GTM judgment and assess what candidates have actually owned and delivered—not just their titles or past employers.

 - You communicate crisply and move with urgency—candidates and stakeholders always know what’s next.

 - You thrive in startup ambiguity, turning loose inputs into clear profiles, assessment plans, and repeatable processes.

 - You pair operational rigor with high standards, thoughtful stakeholder management, and a fast, high-touch candidate experience.

 - You build trust beyond an immediate opening, earning introductions and referrals in close-knit talent communities.

 - You exercise discretion with sensitive information and use AI thoughtfully to reduce repetitive work.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own full-cycle recruiting across Sales, Growth, business development, government relations, partnerships, and customer/mission-facing leadership, based on business priorities.

 - Partner with hiring managers on role outcomes, candidate profiles, interview plans, scorecards, and calibration.

 - Build lasting relationships in cyber, national security, and cleared talent communities through industry events, referrals, and engagement beyond open searches.

 - Tailor structured screens to each role’s proof points, distinguishing commercial results, partnership development, customer trust, and mission credibility.

 - Partner with technical recruiters and subject-matter experts on specialized mission-facing searches, with clear ownership and domain assessment.

 - Lead high-touch closing efforts around Twenty’s mission, the role’s impact, and candidate motivations; surface concerns early.

 - Use market intelligence to advise leaders on role scope, leveling, candidate availability, and realistic search timelines; maintain fast feedback and accurate ATS records.

 - Partner with TAOps on logistics; improve outreach, candidate preparation, and workflows using AI within company guidelines.




MUST HAVE

 - You have 5+ years of recruiting experience, including full-cycle GTM or business hiring in competitive markets.

 - You have recruiting experience in defense technology, cyber, or companies serving government and national security customers.

 - You’ve recruited Sales, business development, partnerships, or customer-facing leaders, with depth in at least one area and range to learn adjacent functions.

 - You’ve built qualified outbound pipelines and closed passive candidates, including senior individual contributors or leaders.

 - You calibrate effectively with hiring managers and learn complex customer and mission contexts quickly.

 - You turn ambiguous hiring needs into executable plans and advise leaders candidly on scope, market realities, and closing.

 - You use funnel data to improve outcomes, with strong ATS hygiene, follow-through, and process discipline.

 - You are comfortable working in-office in Arlington, VA.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Familiarity with government-facing business development, government relations, complex sales cycles, or mission-facing talent.

 - Direct experience recruiting for roles with clearance requirements, including navigating their impact on talent pools, recruiting timelines, and closing.

 - An established network in cyber, defense, national security, or cleared talent communities.

 - Experience building GTM teams at startups or growth-stage companies.

 - Familiarity with Ashby, structured interviewing, and AI-assisted recruiting workflows.




RECRUITING TOOLS (YOU MIGHT WORK WITH)

 - Ashby (ATS, workflows, reporting)

 - LinkedIn Recruiter and Juicebox

 - AI-assisted research, sourcing, and workflow tools within company guidelines

 - Health. Medical, dental, and vision plan options. Life / AD&D, disability coverage options.

 - Family. Paid parental leave for eligible full-time employees. 12 weeks for birthing parents, 4 for non-birthing parents, 6 weeks for adoptive, foster, or intended parents through surrogacy.

 - Vacation. Paid holidays and flexible PTO. Take what you need.

 - Retirement. 401(k) with pre-tax and Roth options. HSA/FSA options, dependent care FSA.
